headline_marked: [[Cabinet approves new pay scale]] for govt employees; salaries to rise 100-142%
headline: Cabinet approves new pay scale for govt employees; salaries to rise 100-142%
summary: The new national pay scale will be implemented in three phases over two fiscal years, benefiting approximately 3.3 million government employees and retirees. It includes significant increases in basic pay, pensions, and new allowances.
details: The Cabinet has approved a new national pay scale for civilian government employees and the armed forces. This decision will see basic salaries increase by 100-142% across different grades, with implementation planned in three phases over two fiscal years, effective from July 1, 2026.

Under the new structure, the lowest grade (20th) will experience a 142% increase, with its basic salary rising from BDT 8,250 to BDT 20,000. For the highest grade (1st), the basic salary will increase by 100%, moving from BDT 78,000 to BDT 156,000.

The implementation will begin with 40% of the new basic pay from July 1, 2026, followed by an additional 30% in January 2027, and the final 30% in July 2027. Various allowances associated with the new pay scale will become effective from January 1, 2028.

This revised pay structure is set to benefit approximately 2.4 million military and civilian government employees, along with over 925,000 retirees, totaling around 3.3 million beneficiaries. The government estimates an additional annual expenditure of BDT 105,580 crore for its implementation.

Pensioners will also receive substantial increases, with their pensions rising by 55% to 100% depending on their current amount. A new disability allowance of BDT 3,000 per month will be introduced for government employees' children with special needs, a first-time provision.

Furthermore, the mobile allowance, previously restricted to Grade 5 and above, will now be extended to all grades. A separate pay structure for the judiciary is currently under review by a committee and will be approved and implemented in phases at a later date.

The government aims to fully implement the 'one grade one pension' system by 2030, acknowledging the significant financial implications and data challenges for retirees from before 2019. The current phased approach is a strategic measure to manage the financial burden effectively.

headline_marked: [[3 Air Force personnel die]] in pickup crash at Dhaka airport’s Third Terminal flyover
headline: 3 Air Force personnel die in pickup crash at Dhaka airport’s Third Terminal flyover
summary: A Bangladesh Air Force pickup truck lost control and plunged from the second-story flyover of Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport's Third Terminal, resulting in multiple casualties.
details: Three Bangladesh Air Force (BAF) personnel were killed and four others injured when a BAF pickup truck met with an accident at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport's Third Terminal. The incident occurred around 10:20 PM on Monday, August 31, during their regular duty.

The Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) confirmed the fatalities, identifying the deceased as Warrant Officer Mahmud, Corporal Pias, and LAC Zubaidul. Their deaths occurred at the scene of the crash.

According to ISPR, the BAF pickup lost control while on duty at the Third Terminal and plunged from the flyover's second floor. The vehicle overturned upon impact, leading to the immediate deaths of the three personnel.

Following the accident, the injured members were promptly transferred to Combined Military Hospital (CMH) in Dhaka for necessary medical treatment. Arrangements are also being made for the post-mortem procedures of the deceased.
